book_title: The Second Epistle of Peter the Apostle.

verses.text: <sc>SIMON PETER</sc> ſeruant and Apoſtle of <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, to them that haue obtained equal faith vvith vs in the iuſtice of our God and Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt.
Grace to you and peace be accompliſhed in the knovvledge of God and Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord:
as al things of his diuine povver vvhich pertaine to life and godlines, are giuen vs by the knovvledge of him vvhich hath called vs by his ovvne propre glorie and vertue,
by vvhom he hath giuen vs moſt great and pretious promiſes: that by theſe you may be made partakers of the diuine nature, fleeing the corruption of that concupiſcence vvhich is in the vvorld.
And you employing al care, miniſter ye in your faith, vertue: and in vertue, knovvledge:
and in knovvledge, abſtinence: and in abſtinence, patience: and in patience, pietie:
and in pietie, loue of the fraternitie: and in the loue of the fraternitie, charitie.
For if theſe things be preſent vvith you, & abound: they ſhal make you not vacant, nor vvithout fruite in the knovvledge of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt.
For he that hath not theſe things ready, is blinde, and groping vvith his hand, hauing forgotten the purging of his old ſinnes.
VVherfore, brethren, labour the more that by good vvorkes you may make ſure your vocation and election. for, doing theſe things, you ſhal not ſinne at any time.
For ſo there ſhal be miniſtred to you aboundantly an entrance into the euerlaſting kingdom of our Lord and Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt.
For the vvhich cauſe I wil begin to admoniſh you alvvaies of theſe things: and you in deede knovving & being confirmed in the preſent truth.
But I thinke it meete as long as I am in this tabernacle, to ſtirre you vp by admonition:
being certaine that the laying avvay of my tabernacle is at hand, according as our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt alſo ſignified to me.
And I vvil doe my diligence, you to haue often after my deceaſe alſo, that you may keepe a memorie of theſe things.

<na>[1]</na> For not hauing folovved vnlearned fables, haue vve made the povver and <na>[2]</na> <alt>`preſence</alt>' of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt knovven to you: but <na>[3]</na> made beholders of his greateneſſe.

notes.text: The Epiſtle in the Transfiguration of our Lord, Aug. 6.
c By this it is plaine, that either Iohn, Iames, or Peter muſt be the author of this epiſtle. for theſe three onely vvere preſent at the Trāsfiguration. Mat. 17, 1.

verses.text: For, [1] he receiuing from God his father honour and glorie, this maner of voice comming dovvne to him from the magnifical glorie, This is my beloued ſonne in vvhom I haue pleaſed my ſelf, heare him.
And this voice vve heard brought from heauen, vvhen vve vvere vvith him in the <na>[1]</na> holy mounte.

notes.text: holy mount. You ſee that places are made holy by Chriſt's preſence, and that all places be not alike holy. See Annot. Act. 7, 33.

verses.text: And we haue the prophetical vvord more ſure: vvhich you doe vvel attending vnto, as to a candel ſhining in a darke place, vntil the day davvne, and the day ſtarre ariſe in your hartes: ⊢
vnderſtanding this firſt that no prophecie of ſcripture is made by priuate interpretation.
For, <cr>[1]</cr> not by mans vvil vvas prophecie brought at any time: but the holy men of God ſpake, inſpired vvith the holy Ghoſt.

chapters.summary: Hovv much God hath done for them, making them Chriſtians : 5 and that they againe muſt doe their part, not hauing onely faith, but al other vertues alſo and good vvorkes, that ſo they may haue the more aſſurance to enter into the kingdom of heauen. 13 And that he is ſo careful to admoniſh them, knovving that his death is at hand, knovving alſo moſt certainly the comming of Chriſt by the vvitnes of the Father him ſelf, as alſo by the Prophets. Concerning vvhom he vvarneth them that they folovv not priuate ſpirites, but the holy Ghoſt ( ſpeaking novv in the Church. )

verses.text: <sc>BVT</sc> there vvere alſo falſe-prophets in the people, as alſo in you there <cr>[1]</cr> ſhal be lying maiſters vvhich ſhal bring in ſectes of perdition, and denie him that hath bought them, <na>[2]</na> the Lord: bringing vpon them ſelues ſpeedie perdition.
And <na>[1]</na> many ſhal folovv their riotouſneſſes, by vvhom the vvay of truth ſhal be blaſphemed.

notes.text: Heretikes ( of vvhom he prophecieth here ) do gaine ſcholers, by preaching libertie, and by their ovvne licentious life ; vvhich is ſpecially ioyned to the hereſie of theſe daies.

verses.text: and in auarice ſhal they <na>[1]</na> vvith feined vvordes make merchandiſe of you. vnto vvhom the iudgement novv long ſince ceaſeth not: and their perdition ſlumbereth not.

notes.text: Al the ſvveete vvordes of heretikes, ſpeaking much of the vvord of the Lord, the Goſpel, IESVS CHRIST &c. are but termes of art to bie and ſel poore mens ſoules.

verses.text: For if God ſpared not Angels ſinning: but with the ropes of Hel being dravven dovvne into Hel deliuered them to be tormented, that they ſhould be reſerued vnto iudgement:
& he ſpared not the original vvorld, but <cr>[1]</cr> kept the eight, Noë, the preacher of iuſtice, bringing in the deluge vpon the vvorld of the impious.
And <cr>[1]</cr> bringing the cities of the Sodomites and of the Gomorrheites into aſhes, he damned them vvith ſubuerſion, putting an example of them that ſhal doe impiouſly:
and <cr>[1]</cr> deliuered iuſt Lot oppreſſed by the iniurie and luxurious conuerſation of the abominable men.
for in ſight and <na>[1]</na> hearing he vvas iuſt: dvvelling vvith them vvho from day to day vexed the iuſt ſoule vvith vniuſt vvorkes.
Our Lord knovveth to deliuer the godly from tentation, but to reſerue the vniuſt vnto the day of iudgement to be tormented:
<na>[1]</na> and eſpecially them vvhich vvalke after the fleſh in concupiſcence of vncleanneſſe, and contemne dominion, bold, ſelf-pleaſers: they feare not to bring in ſectes, blaſpheming.
Vvhereas Angels being greater in ſtrength and povver, beare not the execrable iudgement <na>[1]</na> againſt them.
But theſe men as vnreaſonable beaſtes, naturally tending to the ſnare and into deſtruction, <na>[1]</na> in thoſe things vvhich they know not, blaſpheming, ſhal periſh in their corruption,

notes.text: So heretikes blaſpheme the higheſt myſteries of our faith through ignorance.

verses.text: receiuing the revvard of iniuſtice, eſteeming for a pleaſure the delightes of a day: <na>[1]</na> bcoinquinations and ſpottes, flovving in delicacies, in their feaſtings rioting vvith you,
hauing eies ful of adulterie and inceſſant ſinne: alluring vnſtable ſoules, hauing their hart exerciſed vvith auarice, the children of malediction:
leauing the right vvay they haue erred, hauing folovved the vvay of Balaam of Boſor, vvhich loued the revvard of iniquitie,
but <cr>[1]</cr> had a checke of his madneſſe. the dumme beaſt vnder the yoke, ſpeaking vvith mans voice, prohibited the foliſhnes of the prophet.
Theſe are fountaines vvithout vvater, and cloudes, toſſed vvith vvhirlevvindes, to vvhom the miſt of darkeneſſe is reſerued.
For, ſpeaking the proud things of vanitie, they allure in the deſires of fleſhly riotouſnes, thoſe that eſcape a litle, vvhich conuerſe in errour,
<cr>[1]</cr> promiſing them libertie, vvhereas them ſelues are the ſlaues of corruption. for, <na>[2]</na> vvherevvith a man is ouercome: of that he is the ſlaue alſo.

notes.text: Vvho euer promiſed more libertie to their folovvers then Luther, Caluin, & the like, taking avvay penance, faſting, continencie or chaſtitie, keeping of vovves, neceſſitie of good vvorkes ( becauſe faith doeth al ) obedience to Eccleſiaſtical paſtors and Coūcels, and ſuch like? · Io. 8, 34. Ro. 6, 16.

verses.text: For if fleeing from the coinquinations of the vvorld in the knovvledge of our Lord and Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, they againe intangled vvith the ſame be ouercome: <cr>[1]</cr> the later things are become vnto them vvorſe then the former.
For it vvas better for them not to knovv the vvay of iuſtice, then after the knovvledge, to turne backe from that holy commandement vvhich vvas deliuered to them.
For, that of the true prouerbe is chaunced to them, <cr>[1]</cr> The dogge returned to his vomite: and, The ſovve vvaſhed <na>[2]</na> into her vvallovving in the mire.

chapters.summary: As not onely Prophets, but alſo falſe-prophets vvere in the old Teſtament, ſo novv likevviſe there ſhal be Maiſters of Hereſie, to the damnation of them ſelues, and of their folovvers. 4 And of their damnation he pronounceth by examples ( as he comforteth the vertuous Catholikes or true beleeuers vvith the example of Lot ) becauſe of their railing at their Superiors and Prelates, their blaſpheming of Catholike doctrine, their voluptuous liuing, their lecherie, their couetouſnes, their maner of ſeducing, and the perſons ſeduced, 20 for vvhom it had been leſſe damnable, if they had neuer been Chriſtians.

verses.text: <sc>THIS</sc> loe the ſecond epiſtle I vvrite to you my deereſt, <na>[1]</na> in vvhich I ſtirre vp by admonition your ſincere minde:
that you may be mindeful of thoſe vvordes vvhich I told you before from the holy Prophetes, and of your Apoſtles, of the preceptes of our Lord and Sauiour.
Knovving this firſt, that <cr>[1]</cr> in the laſt daies ſhal come mockers in deceit, vvalking according to their ovvne concupiſcences,
ſaying, Vvhere is his promiſe or his comming? For ſince the time that the fathers ſlept, al things do ſo perſeuere from the beginning of creature.
for they are vvilfully ignorant of this, that the heauens vvere before, & the earth, out of vvater, and through vvater, conſiſting by the vvord of God:
by the vvhich, that vvorld then, being ouerflovved vvith vvater periſhed.
But the heauens vvhich novv are, & the earth, are by the ſame word kept in ſtore, reſerued to fire vnto the day of iudgement & of the perdition of the impious men.
But this one thing be not ignorant of, my deereſt, that <cr>[1]</cr> one day with our Lord is as a thouſand yeres, & a thouſand yeres as one day.
Our Lord ſlacketh not his promis, as ſome do eſteeme it: but he doth patiently for you, <cr>[1]</cr> not vvilling that any periſh, but that al returne to penance.

And <cr>[1]</cr> the day of our Lord ſhal come as a theefe in the vvhich the heauens ſhal paſſe vvith great violence, but the elementes ſhal be reſolued vvith heate, and the earth and the vvorkes vvhich are in it, ſhal be burnt.
Therfore vvhereas al theſe thinges are to be diſſolued: vvhat maner of men ought you to be in holy conuerſations and godlineſſe,
expecting and haſting vnto the comming of the day of our Lord, by vvhich the heauens burning ſhal be reſolued, and the elementes ſhal melt vvith the heate of fire?
But vve expect <cr>[1]</cr> nevv heauens and a nevv earth according to his promiſes, in vvhich iuſtice inhabiteth.
For the vvhich cauſe my deereſt, expecting theſe things, labour earneſtly to be found immaculate and vnſpotted to him in peace:
and <cr>[1]</cr> the longanimitie of our Lord, do ye account ſaluation, as alſo our moſt deere brother Paul according to the vviſedom giuen him hath vvritten to you:

as alſo in al epiſtles, ſpeaking in them of theſe things, in the vvhich are certaine things hard to be vnderſtoode, vvhich the vnlearned and vnſtable depraue, as alſo the reſt of the Scriptures, to their ovvne perdition.
You therefore brethren, foreknovving, take heede leſt ledde aſide by the errour of the vnwiſe you fal away from your owne ſtedfaſtnes.
but grovv in grace and in knovvledge of our Lord and ſauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt. To him be glorie both novv and vnto the day of eternitie. Amen.

chapters.summary: Theſe tvvo Epiſtles he vvriteth to confirme them in the Apoſtles doctrine, and vvarneth them of ſcorners that ſhal come, and denie Domeſday. 5 Whoſe vaine argument he anſvvereth, and giueth the reaſon of Gods ſo long patience, 10 exhorting to al holines of life in reſpect of that terrible day. 16 Finally giuing vvarning of ſuch as miſinterprete S. Paules Epiſtles & the other Scriptures, and that vve muſt not for any thing fall from the true faith.
